parties:
Commissioner of Taxes, Chittagong Zone, Chittagong
Vs.
M/S. Metropolitan Tanneries Ltd.
full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J. This appeal by the Commissioner of Taxes, Chittagong Zone is directed against the judgment and order passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Application No.4 of 1981 under section 66(1) of the Income Tax Act. 

 2. Facts are as follows : The Assessee respondent M/s Metropolitan Tanneries Ltd. a private Limited Company, took loan from the then Commerce Bank (now Agrani Bank) in 1966 and it owned a debt of Taka Fourteen lacs and odd by mortgaging the tannery. Since the Company could not repay the loan had executed an irrevocable General Power of Attorney in favour of the Bank on 3-1-69 to carry on, manage and supervise the business, to lease out the property of the assessee company. The assessee company also entered into an agreement on the same day with the said Commerce Bank for repayment of loan by leasing out the Tanneries to M/s Monti Tanneries Ltd. at an annual rent of Taka two lacs which will be adjusted towards the satisfaction of the debt till the entire loan with interest is liquidated. In pursuance of the agreement the Bank leased out the Tanneries to M/s Monti Tannery Ltd. at an annual rental of Taka two lacs for 10 years on 4-1-69. 

 6. Notwithstanding the aforesaid favourable order an application under section 66(1) was filed before the High Court Division raising two main questions of law: 

 7. A Division Bench of the High Court Division noticed that the Assessment order shows that the assessment was made under section 23(4) /41 of the Act. The learned Judges took the view that the power of Attorney could not be taken as a Trust deed and as such the application under section 41 could not be said to be lawful. It was noticed that a notice under section 34 was upon the principal officer of M/s Metropolitan Tanneries Ltd. C/O the Principal Officer, M/s Agrani Bank Ltd. The learned Judges concluded "so the Income Tax Officer was not sure of the position as to who was to be taxed". The learned Judges rejected the contention of the Revenue that insertion of section 41 was due to a mistake and such mistake will not make the assessment void in view of section 66 of the Income Tax Act. The learned Judges observed: 

 8. Leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division was correct in taking the view as aforesaid. 

 9. This is a case of much a do about nothing. The Assessee respondent company exactly knew what was all about. It filed the appeal before the Appellant Joint Commissioner in his own name (Annexure D). It was represented by a Counsel. It obtained a favourable order from the Assistant Appellate Commissioner. No objection whatsoever was raised on the question of application of section 41 of the Act. It seems only before the Tribunal this technical question was raised and the Tribunal noticed that the Assesses could not make out a case of prejudice and therefore no objection could be taken to the Assessment order. Then the matter was taken up to the High Court Division and the learned Judges, with respect, have taken the view of law which cannot be sustained. The simple truth is that the Assessee company took a loan from the Bank. Since it could not repay the debt, arrangement was made by the respondent company for running its business etc. by the Bank and Power of Attorney was given to that effect and in pursuance of that power of attorney the assessee company's premises were leased out to Monti Tannery, the company who took lease at an annual rent of Taka two lacs and arrangement was that this will be adjusted against the loan of the assessee company. For four years the Bank file return of the Assessee company but only for the year 1970-71 no return was filed. Income Tax Office therefore issued a notice under section 34 direction them to file a return, Assessee company refuse the registered letters and consequently the second notice was issued but this time it was sent C/O The Principal Officer of the Bank directing it to file return of the assessee company as Income Tax Officer took the view that the Bank is managing the affairs of the company in pursuance of a Power of Attorney. Since nothing was done Income Tax Officer assessed under section 23(4) and then mentioned section 41. As against that assessment, as noticed, appeal was filed and favourable order was obtained but no objection was taken as to application of section 41. It is only before the Tribunal that this objection was taken and the Tribunal rejected the contention in view of the fact that no prejudice was caused and invoked section 66B which is as under: 

 It was mentioned before the High Court Division that invocation of section 41 was rather a mistake but even then the High Court Division went to the length of saying that the assessment was made without lawful authority. To say the least, the opinion is not backed by law. Section 41 reads as follows; 

 “In the case of Income, profits or gains chargeable under this act which the Courts of Wards, the Administrators-General, the Official Trustees or any receiver or manager (including any person whatever his designation who in fact manages property on behalf of another appointed by or under any order of a Court or any trustee or trustees appointed under a trust declared by a duly executed instrument in writing whether testamentary or otherwise (including the trustee or trustees under any Wakf deed which is valid under the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, 1913 and entitled to receive on behalf of any person the tax shall be levied upon and recoverable from such Court of Wards, Administrator-General, Official Trustee, receiver or manager or trustee or trustees in the like manner and to the same amount as it would be leviable upon and recoverable from the person on whose behalf such income, profits or. gains are receivable and all the provisions of this Act shall apply accordingly. 

 This section provides a machinery and does not effect the incidence of taxation under the charging section. It has mentioned 5 categories of persons but it is not exhaustive. Viscount Simon in William Versus Singer held that the person charged with tax is neither the trustee nor the beneficiary as such, but the person in actual receipt and control of the income which it is sought to reach. If they are under the control of a guardian or a committee then the I.T.O. can issue such a notice. The object of the Act is to secure for the State a tax and the machinery provided for taxing effectively and expediently where they are found. It is on record that Bank had furnished return for the four years excepting the year in question. The I.T.O. issued the first notice on assessee company but it refused and therefore sent the second notice, this time taking pre-caution by sending it to the Bank and for obvious reasons mentioned section 41. The High Court Division has fallen into an error when it said that the I.T.O. "did not know whom to tax." It is far from it. I.T.O. exactly knew that it was taxing the income of the Metropolitan Tanneries Ltd. who by virtue of its power of attorney authorised the Bank to manage its affairs and the Bank in pursuance of such power of Attorney leased it out to the Monti Tanneries Ltd. Therefore I.T.O. exactly knew that it was taxing the Metropolitan Tannery Ltd. and the Assessment order also said so. The Appellate Joint Commissioner also noticed that the appeal was filed by the Metropolitan Tanneries Ltd. and not by the Bank. In this view of the matter the submissions centering on section 41 are irrelevant and the observation of the High Court Division that, the assessment has become illegal because of mentioning of section 41 does not hold good. The assessee company had obtained a favourable order and that order still stands. 

 10. In the result, therefore this appeal is allowed and order of the High Court Division is set aside. There will be no order as to costs.
